meta.title: File:Lathe-Turned Pillar at Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: A richly finished lathe-turned stone pillar inside the Hoysaleshwara Temple at Halebidu, a 12th-century Hoysala monument dedicated to Shiva. The temple is renowned for its finely carved soapstone architecture and sculptural detailing. This photograph highlights the polished circular mouldings of the pillar, adjoining carved supports and the stone railing overlooking the temple grounds.

meta.title: File:Carved Pillars of Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: A row of intricately carved stone pillars at the Hoysaleshwara Temple in Halebidu, showcasing the refined craftsmanship of Hoysala architecture. The pillars combine geometric mouldings with rounded and faceted sections, while the surrounding stonework carries additional decorative details.

meta.title: File:Lathe-Turned Pillars of Parshvanatha Basadi, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: Parshvanatha Basadi was built in 1133 CE by Boppadeva, son of the Hoysala minister Gangaraja, during the reign of Vishnuvardhana. Dedicated to Jain Tirthankara Parshvanatha, the basadi is renowned for its polished, lathe-turned stone pillars. The closely spaced columns feature numerous circular mouldings and ornamental bands, demonstrating the refined stone craftsmanship of Hoysala-period Jain arc
meta.from: file: File:Lathe-Turned Pillars of Parshvanatha Basadi, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg

meta.title: File:Polished Pillars of Parshvanatha Basadi, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: Parshvanatha Basadi is particularly noted for its elegant lathe-turned pillars, whose polished surfaces feature numerous circular mouldings, bands and ornamental details. Built in 1133 CE during the reign of Vishnuvardhana, the Jain temple demonstrates the sophisticated craftsmanship of Hoysala builders. The closely spaced columns create a rhythmic arrangement throughout the mandapa.
